title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google
content:
In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses.
On Tuesday, the company rolled out a Business Hub that will serve as a place where companies can create business profiles that — in a feature that greatly resembles the kind of profiles that Google and other search engines already offer — allow enterprises to verify and update information about their products and services. The feature is currently in beta.
Eligible companies will also be able to create and launch a specialized business agent, which gives ChatGPT users the ability to ask questions about the business and its products.
“As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI,” the company said on Tuesday. “Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT.”
In a move that calls to mind Google Analytics, the Business Hub will also give users access to limited business insights. These insights will reveal how ChatGPT users interact with their products — including profile views, business mentions, website clicks, and other metrics.
Businesses will have to verify their profiles through a formal process, although the company did not share specifics of what that process would entail. Benji Shomair, OpenAI’s VP of Monetization, told journalists on Monday that there are “multiple verification methods that we use for different types of business in different markets.”
OpenAI previously tried to position ChatGPT as an e-commerce hub by which users could buy products directly. This effort — which used a commission fee system — was viewed as a potentially huge source of revenue and a way to make ChatGPT a more direct Amazon competitor. However, that project ultimately failed to take off and, in March, the company retired the effort, which had even included a “checkout cart” feature.
With the integration of business profiles and intelligence, ChatGPT seems to be attempting to become more like Google, which — since the advent of the internet — has been the place where web users go to understand the companies they want to shop at. It remains to be seen whether this initiative will bear better results than the one that sought to make ChatGPT a direct e-commerce hub.

report.summary: OpenAI launched a beta Business Hub that lets companies create verified ChatGPT business profiles, deploy business agents, and view analytics, pushing ChatGPT further into Google-style discovery.
report.background: AI assistants are increasingly becoming the layer where consumers discover products, compare options, and decide which businesses to trust. Google has long owned this role through Business Profiles and search results, while OpenAI has been experimenting with ways to bring commerce into ChatGPT. An earlier effort to make ChatGPT a checkout and e-commerce hub, complete with a cart and commission fees, failed to gain traction and was retired in March. The new Business Hub reflects a narrower strategy: instead of handling transactions directly, OpenAI wants businesses to manage how they appear inside ChatGPT and to give users a way to ask questions about companies and products. The beta also introduces analytics and verification, echoing familiar search-engine tools while raising questions about trust, ranking, and monetization.
key_points: OpenAI’s Business Hub is in beta and lets eligible companies create business profiles where they can verify and update information about their products and services. The format closely resembles Google Business Profiles, signaling that ChatGPT wants to be a place where users look up companies, not just a chatbot.

Businesses can build specialized business agents that ChatGPT users can question about the company and its offerings. This turns a static profile into an interactive layer, potentially helping customers compare products, ask support-style questions, and get business-specific answers without leaving ChatGPT.

The hub includes limited business insights similar to Google Analytics: profile views, business mentions, website clicks, and other interaction metrics. These analytics give companies a feedback loop for understanding how ChatGPT surfaces and refers to them, which could influence how businesses optimize their presence inside AI assistants.

Companies must verify their profiles through a formal process, though OpenAI has not detailed the steps. An executive said OpenAI uses multiple verification methods depending on business type and market, a sign that trust and fraud prevention will be important as ChatGPT becomes a discovery surface.

The launch marks a strategic pivot after OpenAI’s failed direct-commerce push. Rather than competing with Amazon through checkout and commissions, OpenAI is now competing more with Google’s discovery and business-profile layer, connecting companies to ChatGPT users through profiles, agents, and analytics.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the move validates a shift from chatbots as answer engines to assistants as discovery and business-connection platforms. It puts OpenAI in more direct competition with Google’s local and business search products, while creating a new surface for verification, ranking, and eventually monetization. Developers and businesses will need to treat ChatGPT profiles and agents as a new channel, maintaining structured, accurate product data and monitoring how AI systems describe them. Regular users may get richer, more interactive answers about companies, but they should also expect more business-curated content inside ChatGPT and growing pressure on OpenAI to clearly distinguish neutral answers from promotional or sponsored placements.
report.tools: Watch OpenAI’s Business Hub beta and business-agent features, then compare them with Google Business Profile and Bing Places for Business. For structured data, use Schema.org Organization and Product markup plus Google’s Rich Results Test. To monitor how LLMs describe a brand, consider open-source prompt-testing tools such as Promptfoo and evaluation frameworks like Ragas; these can help teams test business-agent answers and track consistency across model changes.
